cases.summary: USPS "package on hold" email from a look-alike address with a redelivery fee

input.pageTitle: Your package is on hold - Gmail
input.visibleText: Your package is on hold. Pay the $1.99 redelivery fee to release your package within 24 hours.

reasons.explanation: A link pretends to be the Post Office (USPS), but it goes to usps-redelivery.example, not the Post Office (USPS)'s real website.
This looks like an official notice from the Post Office (USPS), but it came from notice@usps-redelivery.example, not one of the Post Office (USPS)'s own email addresses.
The sender's address (notice@usps-redelivery.example) pretends to be the Post Office (USPS), but it isn't the Post Office (USPS)'s real address.
This email says it's from the Post Office (USPS), but none of its links go to the Post Office (USPS)'s real website (one goes to usps-redelivery.example).
It asks you to pay a fee before you get something (a prize or a package), or to pay with gift cards, crypto, or a wire transfer. Real companies don't work this way.
It says a package couldn't be delivered or needs a fee. Fake delivery notices are a very common scam. Check the tracking number on the shipper's real website instead.
It asks for money AND rushes or threatens you. Together, these are a classic scam pattern. Check with the company or agency using a number you already have.
It tries to rush you. Real companies give you time to think.

cases.why: Fake USPS sender and website, a fee to release a package, and a deadline.
